name: DRV8308RHAR
title: Three-phase sensored brushless DC motor controller and FET predriver
summary: The DRV8308 runs a three-phase brushless motor from Hall sensors and drives six external N-channel FETs, with gate current selectable from 10 mA to 130 mA, from an 8.5 V to 32 V supply. It can hold speed in closed loop against a reference clock on CLKIN using Hall or FG-trace feedback, or run open loop from a PWM duty cycle or a register. Commutation is 120° from three Halls, 120° from one Hall once locked, or 180° sinusoidal, with programmable advance. Configuration comes from internal OTP, an external EEPROM or SPI; it adds a 5 V regulator, a current limiter and overcurrent, over- and undervoltage and thermal protection.

pins.name: UHP

pins.name: UHN

pins.name: VHP

pins.name: VHN

pins.name: WHP

pins.name: WHN
pins.function: Hall sensor W, negative input.

pins.name: VSW
pins.function: Switched copy of VM: connected to VM while ENABLE is active. With a series resistor it can bias Hall elements.

pins.name: FGFB
pins.function: Output of the FG amplifier; its feedback network connects between this pin and FGINN_TACH.

pins.name: FGINN_TACH
pins.function: Inverting input of the FG amplifier, joined to the FG trace and its filter. With FGSEL = 3 it takes a logic-level TACH signal instead. When the FG amplifier is not used, FGFB is tied to this pin.

pins.name: FGINP
pins.function: Non-inverting input of the FG amplifier, joined to the FG trace and its filter parts when used.

pins.name: SCLK
pins.function: Serial clock. SPI mode: input, data taken on rising edges, internal pulldown. EEPROM mode: open-drain clock output to the EEPROM CLK pin, needs an external pullup.

pins.name: SCS
pins.function: Serial chip select. SPI mode: input, high selects the interface, internal pulldown. EEPROM mode: open-drain output to the EEPROM CS pin, needs an external pullup.

pins.name: SMODE
pins.function: Serial mode select. Open or grounded: SPI mode. Logic high: EEPROM mode.

pins.name: SDATAI
pins.function: Serial data in. SPI mode: data input with internal pulldown. EEPROM mode: takes data from the EEPROM DO pin.

pins.name: SDATAO
pins.function: Serial data out, open drain. SPI mode: read data. EEPROM mode: drives the EEPROM DI pin and needs an external pullup.

pins.name: FGOUT
pins.function: Open-drain tachometer output, made from the FG amplifier or from the Hall sensors (FGSEL). Needs a pullup to the logic supply.

pins.name: FAULTn
pins.function: Fault flag, open drain, pulled low on a fault such as overcurrent or overtemperature.

pins.name: LOCKn
pins.function: Open-drain flag, low when the speed loop is locked.

pins.name: CLKIN
pins.function: Speed reference clock, used in the Clock Frequency and Clock PWM modes. Internal pulldown.

pins.name: BRAKE
pins.function: Brakes the motor; polarity set by BRKPOL. Internal pulldown.

pins.name: DIR
pins.function: Direction of rotation; polarity set by DIRPOL. Internal pulldown.

pins.name: ENABLE
pins.function: Turns the motor driver on and off; polarity set by ENPOL. Internal pulldown.

pins.name: RESET
pins.function: High resets all internal logic. Internal pulldown. May be grounded when not used.

pins.name: VREG
pins.function: 5 V regulator output, on while ENABLE is active. Bypass to GND with 0.1 µF, 10 V ceramic. Can supply the Hall sensors.

pins.name: VINT
pins.function: Bypass for the internal 1.8 V core regulator: 1 µF, 6.3 V ceramic to GND.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground. Pin 26 and the exposed pad are joined inside; both go to board ground.

pins.name: VM
pins.function: Motor supply. Bypass to GND with 0.1 µF ceramic plus a bulk electrolytic of 47 µF or more rated 1.5 to 2.5 times VM.

pins.name: VCP

pins.name: CP2

pins.name: CP1

pins.name: ISEN

circuits.title: Typical application: sensored BLDC drive from 24 V
circuits.description: A 24 V supply feeds VM and the drains of three high-side N-channel FETs; the three low-side FET sources meet at ISEN and return to ground through a 0.03 Ω sense resistor, the current-limit and overcurrent sensing point. Each gate output drives one FET and each phase pin watches its half-bridge midpoint, which also carries one motor lead. The charge pump has 0.1 µF across CP1-CP2 and 1 µF from VCP to VM; VM has 0.1 µF and 470 µF to ground, VINT 1 µF and VREG 0.1 µF. Three Hall elements are biased in parallel from VSW through 1.3 kΩ, returning to ground through 180 Ω, and each output pair has 0.1 µF across it. The FG trace is AC-coupled by 0.1 µF and 2 kΩ into FGINN_TACH, with 820 kΩ parallel 100 pF feedback from FGFB, 1 nF across the trace and 4.7 µF from FGINP to ground. RESET, SMODE and the pad go to ground; a controller drives the SPI pins, CLKIN, BRAKE, DIR and ENABLE and reads SDATAO, FGOUT, FAULTn and LOCKn.

parts.note: pickup winding drawn on the motor board

notes: The controller pulls up the four open-drain lines SDATAO, FGOUT, FAULTn and LOCKn; no resistor values are given for them.
Each FET has its body diode; no part numbers are given for the FETs or the Hall elements.

circuits.title: External EEPROM configuration
circuits.description: With SMODE pulled to VREG the serial port becomes a master that reads the register set out of a Microwire EEPROM of the 93C46B type, 16-bit words. VREG powers the EEPROM. SCLK goes to the EEPROM clock and SCS to its chip select, each with a 10 kΩ pullup to VREG because the DRV8308 drives them open drain in this mode. The EEPROM data output goes to SDATAI; SDATAO, also open drain with a 10 kΩ pullup, goes to the EEPROM data input. VREG keeps its own bypass capacitor and the EEPROM has one at its supply pin.

parts.note: EEPROM supply bypass, value not given

notes: The terminals are DRV8308 pins of the same names. The EEPROM data begin at address 0 in the register order; bits 12 to 15 of each word are unused.

circuits.title: Hall element on one Hall input pair
circuits.description: A Hall element with a differential output of about 100 mV is powered from VREG and ground; its positive output goes to xHP and its negative output to xHN. A capacitor across the pair, usually 1 nF to 100 nF, filters PWM noise and may be left out. VREG keeps its bypass capacitor. The same network repeats for the U, V and W pairs.
notes: x stands for U, V or W.

circuits.title: Open-drain digital Hall sensor on one Hall input pair
circuits.description: A digital Hall sensor with an open-drain output runs from VREG. Its output goes to xHP with a pullup to VREG. Two resistors from VREG to ground bias xHN at 2.5 V, and that node is shared with the xHN inputs of the other two pairs. All three resistors are 1 kΩ to 4.7 kΩ. VREG keeps its bypass capacitor.
notes: x stands for U, V or W; the bias pair on xHN serves all three negative inputs.

operation.text: A predriver and speed controller for three-phase sensored brushless motors. It commutates from three Hall inputs and drives six external N-channel FETs with about 10 V of gate-source drive at a programmable peak current of 10 mA to 130 mA. The die carries a charge pump for the high-side gates, a 5 V regulator, a 1.8 V core regulator, a switched VM output, an FG amplifier and comparator, Hall comparators, OTP memory, an SPI port, a 100 MHz oscillator and a thermal sensor. Package: 6 mm × 6 mm 40-pin QFN, 0.5 mm pitch; ambient range -40 °C to 85 °C.

SPDMODE picks one of three. Clock Frequency Mode is closed loop: the loop drives the FG frequency to match the CLKIN frequency. Clock PWM Mode is open loop: the duty cycle of CLKIN sets the drive. Internal Register PWM Mode is open loop: SPEED/4095 sets the duty. Motor speed is changed by the duty cycle applied to the FETs.

CLKIN is synchronised and deglitched on the internal clock (a level must hold for two consecutive CLK50 edges). A speed comparator weighs CLKIN against the FG signal (from the FG amplifier, the TACH input or the Halls) and issues UP and DOWN pulses. An integrator adds or subtracts SPDGAIN on every integrator clock (CLK50 divided per INTCLK) while UP or DOWN is active; it saturates rather than wrapping and is cleared at reset, on disable and during braking. With no CLKIN edges after ENABLE the integrator stays at zero and the motor is not driven; if CLKIN stops while running, DOWN pulses brake the motor to a stop.

After the integrator comes a one-pole, one-zero digital filter (pole about 100 Hz to 1600 Hz via FILK1, zero 2 Hz to 100 Hz via FILK2, bypassed by BYPFILT) and a lead compensator (COMPK1, COMPK2; centre 20 Hz to 100 Hz, lead 0° to 80°, bypassed by BYPCOMP). Both reset to zero whenever the motor is disabled. LOOPGAIN sets the overall gain.

The incoming PWM is timed against a 50 MHz clock into a 12-bit duty value; 16 kHz to 50 kHz is the intended input range, and higher frequencies lose resolution. The output PWM frequency is separate and set by PWMF to 25, 50, 100 or 200 kHz: lower frequencies cut switching loss, higher ones give finer control at high motor speed. In sine commutation the duty is multiplied by per-phase modulation values; in 120° commutation the modulation is fixed by MOD120.

AUTOGAIN scales LOOPGAIN with CLKIN frequency and AUTOADV scales ADVANCE with Hall_U frequency, for motors run over a wide speed range on one parameter set; both are meant to stay off for single-speed use. Both values latch when LOCK asserts. Together they widen the usable speed range by up to 4×.

Three differential comparators with hysteresis centred on zero detect the Hall crossings. After each valid edge further edges are ignored for 20 µs so PWM noise does not cause false commutation. If noise still gets through, capacitors can go across each input pair and from the inputs to ground. Each Hall input has an ESD diode to VREG, so no Hall input may exceed VREG; since VREG is off in standby, externally powered Hall sensors must be off while the part is in standby and powered before the motor is enabled, or an invalid Hall state can delay start-up.

The FG amplifier's output is on FGFB, so its gain and filtering are set by outside parts; it feeds a comparator whose result also goes to the speed loop. FGSEL chooses the FG source: HALL_U, the XOR of the three Halls, the FG amplifier, or a logic TACH on FGINN_TACH. FGOUT is open drain and needs a pullup to the logic rail.

An FG pickup is often a serpentine trace on the motor board giving a small sine wave whose amplitude and frequency rise with speed. It sits next to the windings, and noise coupled into it spoils regulation, most of all at start-up when the FG signal is near zero and the loop reads noise as speed, so the motor starts slowly; watching FGOUT during start-up shows this. A capacitor across the feedback resistor sets a low-pass pole (example: 36 pulses per revolution at 5000 RPM is 3 kHz, so a pole at 3 kHz rejects 25 kHz PWM); since FG amplitude grows with speed the pole may sit lower. The trace is AC-coupled through 100 nF to 1 µF (6.3 V ceramic is enough) large enough for reliable start-up, and an optional 330 pF to 2200 pF across the trace rejects PWM glitches. Final values come from testing on the motor.

ENPOL in OTP sets the ENABLE polarity (0: active high) and cannot be changed by a register write during operation. Making ENABLE inactive resets the speed loop and brakes or coasts the motor per BRKMOD. Once FGOUT shows no edges for 1 s the part enters standby: all gate outputs low (FETs off), gate-drive regulator, charge pump, VREG and VSW off, analog circuits in low power; digital logic and the serial port keep working.

All internal logic resets at power-up, when VM falls below VRESET, and when RESET is high while ENABLE is active. With ENABLE inactive and RESET high, registers read back as 1. RESET is deglitched by 10 µs on both edges and may be grounded if unused.

Removing ENABLE (held inactive for at least 1.2 µs, or an ENPOL change) starts a stop-and-power-down sequence that runs to completion whatever ENABLE does next: the motor brakes or coasts, and 1 s after rotation stops the internals, the 5 V regulator and power switch power down and clocks stop. Re-asserting ENABLE at once lets the motor slow and stop for 1 s and then restart. RESET asserted during power-down acts when ENABLE returns. RESET asserted while enabled stops the motor the same way, then after 1 s reloads registers from OTP, clears faults and initialises internal state; the motor stays off until RESET falls. With ENPOL programmed active low, RESET and ENABLE can be tied: both low runs the motor, both high stops it, and returning high reloads OTP and clears faults.
A 100 MHz master oscillator, divided to a nominal 50 MHz, times all digital logic.

Three modes: 120° using all three Halls, 120° using HALL_U alone, and 180° sine-wave drive. Direction is DIR XOR DIRPOL; reversing while the motor spins can cause excess current in the output stage. Three-Hall 120° commutation is combinational; misplaced sensors show up as noise, vibration and torque ripple, which single-Hall timing can reduce.

A timer runs at 960 times the HALL_U frequency to time commutation from that one input. It is used only with BASIC = 0 and once the speed is steady and the loop locked (LOCK, also driven out on LOCKn); except in PWM input modes LOCK is withheld while the integrator is saturated. Until lock (start-up, stop, sudden load) 3-Hall 120° commutation runs, so all three Halls are always needed. ADVANCE shifts commutation relative to the Hall edges in 1/960 steps, only in single-Hall modes. Sine mode (ENSINE = 1, BASIC = 0) modulates each phase with a 12-bit pattern approximating sinusoidal current, with transitions midway between Hall edges; MOD120 should then be 3970.

LOCK needs the Hall_U period to be below MINSPD (2.56 ms per count, up to 652.8 ms), period-to-period variation within SPEEDTH (1/4 to 1/512 of a revolution), and then SPDREVS further Hall_U periods. HALLRST sets how many HALL_U edges pass between commutation counter resets (1, 2, 4 or 8). During spin-up in Clock Frequency Mode, before lock, SPEED acts as the open-loop gain.

The internal speed loop works best at electrical speeds of about 50 Hz to 6.7 kHz (about 500 RPM to over 100000 RPM for 8 poles); outside that it still runs with weaker regulation, especially on Hall feedback. One parameter set covers a limited range (for example 1000 RPM to 2000 RPM); SPI updates are allowed while running. In sine commutation the 25-bit, 50 MHz commutation timer captures at most 655 ms, setting a minimum of about 1.5 Hz (23 RPM, 8 poles), and the 960 steps per cycle set a maximum of 52 kHz (800000 RPM, 8 poles). PWM-input and register modes with 3-Hall commutation have no speed limits.

Braking comes from BRAKE XOR BRKPOL: all low-side gates turn on and the integrator is cleared. BRKMOD chooses brake (1) or coast with 3-stated outputs (0) for RESET, ENABLE inactive, DIR and power-down; BRAKE active and a missing clock always brake.

Each gate output is a CMOS buffer for an external N-channel FET. The high-side output goes to VCP when the phase's PWM is high, the commutation enables the high side and the current limit is not tripped; the low-side output goes to VM when the commutation selects it or, with SYNRECT = 1, when the high side is off. Asynchronous rectification lets current recirculate through diodes or FET body diodes; synchronous rectification usually gives better speed control and efficiency. During one side's turn-on the opposite gate is clamped off through a low impedance so its gate-source capacitance cannot turn it on. An analog dead time is always enforced and DTIME adds digital dead time.

IDRIVE sets the peak gate current, 10 mA to 130 mA, which sets the output slew rate together with the FET's gate charge. The peak current flows for TDRIVE (1, 5, 10 or 15 µs) after each transition, then a weak source holds the gate. The current must be large enough to finish charging or discharging the gate within TDRIVE, or the FET dissipates heavily. The 10 mA setting switches about 5 times slower than 50 mA. Fast edges add noise on VM and ground, worsened by slow low-side body-diode recovery; 10 mA has suited many FETs running below 5 A.

When the voltage on the low-side sense resistor exceeds VLIMITER (0.25 V typical) the high-side FET turns off until the next PWM cycle, with the low-side FET on if synchronous rectification is enabled. A blanking time (tBLANK, set by OCPDEG) after each PWM turn-on masks the comparator. Limiting spin-up current this way reduces the bulk capacitance needed.
Generates about VM + 10 V for the high-side gates using a flying capacitor between CP1 and CP2 and a storage capacitor from VCP to VM. It is off in standby.

VREG supplies internal logic and outside loads such as Hall sensors, up to 30 mA subject to dissipation, and always needs its 0.1 µF, 10 V ceramic to ground even when unloaded. It is off in standby unless VREG_EN = 1. VSW is a low-current switch from VM, on while ENABLE is active, for Hall sensors or other loads.
Each protection pulls FAULTn low and sets its bit in the FAULT register (0x2A). Bits stay set until written 0, RESET is asserted or power is cycled. UVLO and CPFAIL are set at power-up.

Below VUVLO the driver is disabled and FAULTn pulled low; above it FAULTn releases and driving resumes on its own. Registers stay accessible during UVLO as long as VM is above the reset threshold; below it all registers reset.

Energy returned from the load through synchronous rectification can pump up VM. Above the OVTH-selected threshold (34.5 V or 28 V) FAULTn goes low and synchronous rectification falls back to asynchronous; once VM is back below the threshold FAULTn releases and, 60 µs later, synchronous rectification returns. The FETs must be rated above the chosen threshold.

Independent of the current limit, the drain-source voltage of every driven FET is monitored; above VFETOCP (OCPTH) for longer than tOCP (OCPDEG) an OCP event is raised. A voltage on ISEN above VSENSEOCP also raises one. The driver is disabled with FAULTn low and re-enabled after a fixed 5 ms.

If VCP falls below VCPFAIL (about VM + 3 V) the driver is disabled until it recovers, and CPFAIL is set. A short on the charge pump disables it and the driver; after 5 s operation retries, repeating while the short remains.
Above TTSD the device is disabled with FAULTn low and OTS set. With RETRY = 1 it re-enables 5 s after cooling below the threshold; with RETRY = 0 the predrivers stay off until RESET or a power cycle.

Registers load at power-up from OTP (SMODE low) or from an external Microwire EEPROM (SMODE high, the port then acting as master and latching data on falling SCLK). Three set-ups are possible: a preprogrammed EEPROM; SPI writes while powered; or SPI writes then a one-time burn into OTP. To program an EEPROM in circuit, hold RESET high so the serial pins 3-state; the DRV8308 cannot program an EEPROM itself. OTP can be burned once and can still be overridden by SPI or EEPROM afterwards.

Each access is 24 bits: a read/write bit, 7 address bits and 16 data bits, shifted in while SCS is high and latched into the addressed register when SCS falls. Any pause between bits is allowed while SCS stays high, so byte-wide transfers work, and clock edges after the 24th are ignored. For a read only the address is taken from SDATAI and the 16 data bits come out on SDATAO.

Six N-channel FETs, chosen for pulsed and continuous drain current, VDS above VM, VGS rating of at least 12 V (the gate drive is about 10 V) and low RDS(on) for lower temperature. Larger FETs with more gate charge need higher IDRIVE settings.
A Hall element's output scales with its bias current; VREG or VSW with a series resistor sets that current, sized from the elements' resistance (series or parallel) and, with VSW, from VM.

Run from a well-regulated 8.5 V to 32 V supply with at least 47 µF of bulk capacitance on VM. Place the 0.1 µF VM bypass close to the device with a small VM-to-GND loop. Solder the exposed pad to the board for thermal and mechanical performance.
